h1: The Assumption of Mary: Fourth Glorious Mystery
intro: A little read-aloud book for one decade of the Rosary: The Assumption of Mary.
shortAnswer: This book walks children through the Fourth Glorious Mystery, the Assumption of Mary: a short story, the Gospel passage, the Our Father, ten Hail Marys and the Glory Be, and a reflection on devotion to Mary and purity of heart.
aboutHtml:
Painting: Titian, Assumption (Frari), detail crop. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons. Image source (Wikimedia Commons).

The Gospel passage is quoted word for word from the Douay-Rheims Bible, 1899 American Edition, which is in the public domain; verse numbers are omitted for reading aloud, and … marks skipped verses. The Our Father, Hail Mary, Glory Be and Fatima prayers follow the standard formulas used across this site. This mystery is traditionally prayed on Wednesday / Sunday.

The Church teaches that Mary was assumed body and soul into heaven (Pope Pius XII, Munificentissimus Deus, 1950); the passage on the Gospel page is the traditional sign from the Book of Revelation.

faq.q: What is the Fourth Glorious Mystery?
faq.a: The Assumption of Mary. When Mary's life on earth was finished, God brought her, body and soul, into the glory of heaven. This mystery is traditionally prayed on Wednesday / Sunday, and its fruit is devotion to Mary and purity of heart.

faq.q: How do you pray this decade with children?
faq.a: Read one page at a time. On the decade page, pray the Our Father once, the Hail Mary ten times (one for each bead), then the Glory Be and the Fatima prayer.
